In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the deuteron data obtained in the PAM-ELA experiment are in good agreement with the data of other experiments and with the predictions of theoretical models of albedo particle fluxes.
the PAMELA results are not consistent with the predictions of the conventional models, and that the observed flux is higher than the expected one by a factor of 1.5–2.5.
the PAMELA results on the deuteron fluxes and the deuteron-to-proton ratio in the albedo are in good agreement with the results obtained by other experiments.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the measured albedo deuterium fluxes at the Earth are in good agreement with the theoretical predictions of the model developed at the Institute for Nuclear Research, RAS, Moscow.
the measured albedo deuteron spectra are well described by a power law in energy.
the PAMELA instrument is a very powerful tool for measuring albedo deuterium fluxes in the near-Earth region.
The main takeaway from our work is that
